title: Agents can colour text by palette name
body:
Agent text reaches coax as markdown and is drawn through cmr. Markdown has no way to colour text, so an agent cannot mark a word red or green. coax already has a palette in `config.toml` with 11 names (accent, muted, selection, foreground, red, yellow, orange, green, cyan, blue, magenta). It maps cmr's code colours through those names in `screen_style` in `src/ui.rs`.

## Proposal

- Agents colour text by palette name, never by hex value, so the colours follow Jack's theme and stay readable on it. An unknown name renders as plain text.
- cmr learns an inline colour syntax and returns the colour as a name. coax maps the name through the palette.
- The coax output style (coax-3d286f) lists the syntax and the names. It says when colour helps: status words, warnings, summaries of what passed and what failed. It is not for decoration.

## Open

- The syntax. Candidates are a pandoc-style span, as in `[failed]{.red}`; a short tag of coax's own, as in `{red|failed}`; or an HTML span, which cmr would have to parse and the output style bans today. Outside coax, in Claude Code or another client, the markup shows as typed.
- coax-1898d3 (links with a hover popup and a decade action) also needs an inline syntax of coax's own. The two should share one form, for example `[text]{.red}` and `[text]{foam=coax-12e8af}`.
- Whether colour can nest with bold or code, and whether a coloured span can cross a line break.
